approach: Add two entries to `defaults.toml` (`version-pins`, `hermetic-checks`) in the file's real shape: `id`, `statement`, `applies_to`, `source`. The brief says `classes` and `text`, but `Default` in `crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs:17-23` has `deny_unknown_fields`, so those names would fail to parse. `DefaultsModel::render` (defaults.rs:58-72) shows the reader only the first sentence of each statement (`first_sentence`, defaults.rs:77-83). So each statement's first sentence carries the whole stance: exact, never auto-floated, ambient. Later sentences add detail for the producer and verifier, who get the full text through `get`. The `version-pins` entry names the existing `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` command from D154. `xtask/src/main.rs` has it (13 `repin` matches), so nothing is built. Raise `BudgetSet::Reader` from 2_000 to 2_200 in `crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:176`, with a comment saying why. The entries add about 170 tokens against 2 tokens of headroom, and defaults are always loaded into the reader set (lib.rs:286). Make the hardcoded "of 2000" at `run_pin_tests.rs:1625` read `BudgetSet::Reader.budget()`. Update the `budget reader` line in `docs/system-facts.md`, because `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (`crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs:125`) fails otherwise. That file is not a listed deliverable, but the test forces the edit. Add one new test in defaults.rs that parses the real file and checks, by a table of (id, classes, key phrases), that each stance is in both the full statement and the rendered reader line. It also renders the defaults for class `code` and `config` the way the reader sees them, which covers criterion 7. Append D181 to `docs/decisions.md` and a CHANGELOG entry. The version in defaults.toml stays 1: nothing in the loader requires a bump (`parse` checks only duplicates and empties, defaults.rs:36-49), and earlier added entries did not bump it.

decisions.choice: Put the whole stance in each entry's first sentence. Later sentences hold only extra detail: the repin command name, and the rule for recording a tool choice.
decisions.reason: The reader loads only the first sentence (`render` and `first_sentence`, defaults.rs:55-83). A key phrase placed after the first full stop would never reach the reader, so the reader would still ask.

rejected.option: One long statement with the phrases spread across several sentences
rejected.why: The reader would see only the first sentence, so the defect that caused both jobs would remain.
That would raise the reader set by far more than 170 tokens and change every default's rendering. The existing tests pin the first-sentence form (defaults.rs:100-126, 129-145).

decisions.choice: Raise the reader budget to 2_200 and update `docs/system-facts.md` to the computed size. The test hardcode at run_pin_tests.rs:1625 reads `BudgetSet::Reader.budget()`.
decisions.reason: The brief requires the raise. The set has 2 tokens of headroom (1998 of 2000, `docs/system-facts.md:25`). The two entries cost about 170 tokens by my estimate (~510 bytes at ⌈bytes/3⌉). The producer must measure the real figure and set the budget to the smallest round value above it with a small margin, not above 2_200 unless measured. D170 says budgets never rise to fit a set, so D181 records this as a deliberate exception: the content is policy that stops a user question, and nothing is left to trim.

rejected.option: Pay with removals from reader.md or the catalog
rejected.why: Both are outside the listed deliverables, and D170 already trimmed the reader prompt to its limit.

rejected.option: Keep the 2000 literal in run_pin_tests.rs and edit it to 2200
rejected.why: A literal drifts the next time the budget moves; reading the `BudgetSet` value removes the duplicate.

decisions.choice: Apply `version-pins` to code, config and build, as the brief requires. Apply `hermetic-checks` to code, config, build and tests.
decisions.reason: The classes are the ones the reader matches a request against. Hermetic checks are mostly tests and gates, so `tests` is named for them. `rust` and `tested` already use these class names.

rejected.why: Every reading would then carry both stances as criteria, including docs-only requests, and the reader would be asked to apply them where they do not fit.

decisions.reason: `DefaultsModel::parse` does not look at the version beyond the type (defaults.rs:36-49). `behavior-evidence`, `outcome-check`, `no-empty-success` and `thrash-stop` were added without a bump. The only test that reads it asserts `>= 1` (defaults.rs:94).

rejected.why: It would change the rendered header with no consumer that needs it.

decisions.reason: Criteria 5 and 7 require the property to hold for the class of request, not only for p806's wording. The table also fails if a stance is moved out of the first sentence.

If the figure is above 2200, the producer shortens the sentences before raising the budget further, and records the final figure in D181 and `docs/system-facts.md`.
